felix: Quick summary from today's micro-window run: host parse + tokenize accounts for ~12% of p95 on small chats after we turned on frame-coalescer.
anya: Stack top?
felix: parse_frames -> reassemble_stream -> tokenize_accumulate -> utf8_normalize -> kvcache_lookup.
anya: Interesting that kvcache shows latency bumps too. Did coalescer merge mixed-length windows?
felix: Yes. coalescer merged fragments from short and long requests into the same micro-batch; seq stddev jumped and kernel_selector chose the conservative fallback kernel more often. p95 decode CPU up ~14%.
tom: Any kvcache metrics?
felix: per-batch lookup volume +20%, miss rate +2.2%, per-lookup latency +45us during spike windows. Eviction bursts aligned with the worst tail events.
anya: Could be feedback loop: mixed batches -> conservative kernel -> longer preproc -> more coalescing backlog -> worse mixing.
julia: Two immediate fixes: 1) add seq-bucketing to the coalescer so it won't merge streams whose length histograms differ by > factor 4, 2) clamp variance before kernel decision (clip outliers at p90) so a single long request doesn't force fallback.
felix: Implemented quick sim: bucketing cut mixed batches by 72%, kernel clamp reduced fallback picks by 58%, p95 host parse down ~9% in sim.
tom: Tokenization micro-optimizations?
felix: pre-reserve token buffer + ascii-fastpath. Pre-reserve reduced tokenize_accumulate median 0.38ms -> 0.12ms in microbench. ascii fastpath skipped normalize for ~65% of payloads and saved ~0.14ms median.
anya: Memory tradeoffs? pre-reserve raises per-worker RSS on dense hosts. Use pooled slab with per-worker cap and a recycle window. Add guard metric.
julia: Also introduce a per-batch KV lookup budget: once budget exceeded, skip remote lookups and use model-estimated fallbacks. This avoids tail amplification from kvcache storms.
tom: HTTP vs gRPC difference?
felix: grpc p95 host parse ~1.7ms, http/1.1 ~3.0ms in the window. Small header writes and chunked body reassembly are the big cost on http1.
anya: Short-term: enable header-frag coalesce + prefer keepalive and writev merging at ingress. Longer-term: shift high-frequency routes to http/2 or add an ingress coalescing proxy that stitches smallwrites.
julia: Runbook: A) land coalescer bucketing + tests (anya), B) kernel variance clamp flag (tom), C) pre-reserve + pooled slab behind flag + mem cap metric (felix), D) KV per-batch budget + metric (julia), E) ingress header coalesce toggle (infra).
felix: I'll open PRs for (C) and include microbench artifacts and memory graphs.
tom: I'll add the clamp as a runtime flag so we can toggle and add "kernel_mispredict_rate" metric.
anya: I'll prototype bucketing and add "mixed_batch_rate" tracing span.
julia: I'll implement KV budget in the selector path; adds conservative fallback when budget exhausted.
ingsress-bot: deploy-log: canary started at 1765439950, profile: 20% canary.
felix: Note: when enabling pre-reserve, set per-worker cap to 8KB and recycle window 60s, adjust if RSS climbs on density nodes.
julia: Good call. Also watch per-shard kvcache pressure if affinity changes; might need TTL tuning.
tom: target: land behind flags in 48h, canary 24-48h, measure host_parse_p95, kernel_mispredict_rate, kvcache_eviction_spikes.
anya: If we get host_parse_p95 < 1.2ms for small chats we should recover ~6% of tail.
felix: ok, PRs incoming. will attach flame traces. :rocket:
